newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Zaire army pledges loyalty amid unease over Mobutu.
newsitem.headline: Zaire army pledges loyalty amid unease over Mobutu.

text.p: Zaire's military pledged loyalty on Monday to the institutions governing the country's democratic transition amid uncertainty following President Mobutu Sese Seko's prostate surgery in Europe.
A military statement broadcast on state radio appeared intended to defuse persistent rumour about a possible army coup in the event of a vacuum created by Mobutu's absence.

"The military high command rejoices at the success of the surgery on the supreme commander of the Zairean armed forces and congratulates him on his good convalescence," said the statement read out by a military spokesman.

"The military high command affirms its support for the electoral calender for free and transparent elections and asks foreign countries to assist Zaire in organising the elections in peace and transparence," it said.
Mobutu has told the nation he is resting in Switzerland after the operation and plans to return home in the near future.
Speaking by telephone from Lausanne, he told state television on Friday he was no longer under medical supervision.

Mobutu, 66 on October 14, seized power in 1965 in Africa's sprawling equatorial heart. He ruled virtually unchallenged in the chaotic nation until 1990 when opposition protests and pressure from Zaire's foreign partners forced him along the path of democratic reform.
Elections are scheduled to take place by July next year under the transition programme.
